cues.en: So the next image component
is one pretty useful feature
NextJS offers you that can help you optimize
your NextJS websites and optimize the performance
of those websites.
Another pretty useful feature is how NextJS supports you
with adding metadata to your pages.
Metadata that's, for example,
picked up by search engine crawlers,
and that therefore, determines how your website shows up
in such crawlers.
And again, there is a lot you can configure
depending on your exact use cases, and therefore, again,
you might wanna browse the according
official documentation article to learn all about
how you can set up metadata
and which configuration options NextJS offers you here.

of setting up metadata, static metadata and dynamic metadata
in this section now.
[Maximilian Schwarzmüller] So how can you add metadata
to NextJS pages?
Well, the most straightforward way of adding metadata
is to go to a page where you want to add it
and typically, you should add metadata to all your pages
and then in that page.js file,
you export a constant called metadata
and it must be called metadata
and it must be in a page.js file or a layout.js file,
as you will see soon, and it must be exported.
Now this metadata constant then should hold an object,
and that object can hold a couple of different properties
that you can configure.
Most importantly, you can set a title
and a description property here.

which for example, also will show up here in your tabs,
but which will also show up
when your page is displayed as a search result
on Google, for example.
So here for this page where I display my latest posts,
the title could, for example, be latest posts.
The description then is some metadata text,
which for example, shows up here below the title
when your page is displayed in search results.
So here we could say, browse our latest posts.
With that, if you then save that
and you load the page where you added the metadata,
in my case, the starting page here,
you'll see that the title is indeed reflected
here in the tab and you can also see
that metadata text you added that description text
if you go to the head tag of the loaded page.
And then there you should see that description meta element,
which contains that description text
and that's the text that, for example,
would show up in search results.
Now, you can also add more fields than just title
and description to this exported metadata object

and shows you all the different values
and fields you can add here
and attached you find a link to that document.
You can, for example, also add a open graph setting
to this metadata object, which controls the metadata
that will be used when you share a page on X or Facebook.

as a preview if you share a link to your page and so on.
So these are all settings you can set up
on that metadata object,
which is exported with that metadata constant.
Now static metadata
as we have it here is often all you need
because for many pages,
the metadata you wanna set might indeed be static
and not change depending on what's shown on the page.
But you also might have some pages
where the metadata does change
and does depend on the dynamic content of the page.
For example, here in my feed folder,
in the page.js file there, I'm showing all my posts.

here as well, with a title of All Posts
and a description that could be, browse all our posts.

But you also might have some dynamic metadata
on some pages, so some metadata that's not always the same,
but that instead should change
as the data on the page changes.

browse all our X posts,

but by instead exporting a function
called generateMetadata.

for a constant named metadata
or a variable that doesn't matter,
but it must be named metadata, NextJS is looking
for a function named generateMetadata like this
in your page.js files.
And if NextJS then finds such a exported function
with that exact name, it will execute that function
for you when it renders that page.
Now this function will then automatically receive
a configuration object or a data object,
whatever you want to call it.
It will receive that object automatically
because this object with its data
will be passed in by NextJS.

for this page so that you could retrieve dynamic data
if you were on a dynamic page.

that might be set in case these kinds
of information pieces are important to you
for generating the dynamic metadata.

any params or anything like that

I don't have a dynamic route segment here.
